Do not add a production CommunityNoteLoader, general ranked-Hook schema, Dashboard/MCP surface, or LangGraph node merely to make an arm runnable. ### Directional cases and observations Use a small set frozen before first result collection, with a target maximum of 12 cases only when the ground truth can be established from current source/API, tests, or traceable authentic history. Cases used to tune smoke v5 are excluded. Keep code/exact, current-SymbolIndexer-compatible, and community/history strata separate; do not average non-applicable arms into one headline score. Record per case: - correct file found at 5; - correct Hook/symbol found at 5 where the current arm can represent it; - first correct result rank and MRR; - irrelevant returned-file count; - community hint found, then verified, rejected, or unresolved by current source; - latency; - implementation effort and estimated maintenance burden, explicitly not an observed long-term maintenance cost. Absolute case counts may guide the next investment. Small-sample percentages, H1-H5 pass/fail labels, statistical significance, cross-project superiority, wrong-file modification, final Agent success, and production promotion are outside this pilot. ### Time box and stop rules Stop the pilot when any of these occurs: - one working day is exhausted; - an arm needs more than 90 minutes of new platform contract/schema work; - an arm requires LangGraph, Dashboard, MCP, production loader, Dense, RRF, or Agentic expansion; - a frozen-case defect invalidates the run; retain the invalid result and create a new version rather than editing in place; - raw A/B/D results, manual judgments, limitations, and the next-step decision are saved. After the directional report, return to product capability delivery. Collect wrong-target, proposal-review, task-success, retry, and maintenance outcomes in real product work. Open another bounded experiment only when those observations create a concrete decision that cannot be made from existing evidence. ## 2. Conditional Formal-Validation Questions These are the long-term questions that separate bounded experiments may answer when a product decision triggers them. `V2-RET-DIRECTIONAL-001` answers only the A/B/D next-investment subset defined in section 1.2. 1. How much does BM25 improve Recall@K over `rg`-only, and on which source types? 2. How many additional correct Hooks does dense retrieval find beyond BM25 and deterministic code retrieval? 3. Does source-aware mixed retrieval reduce wrong-file modification rate? 4. Does Agentic query rewrite/retry improve final task success? 5. What latency, token/API usage, and monetary cost does each improvement add? 6. How often do code indexes return stale, renamed, deleted, or branch-mismatched results? ## 3. Formal Evaluation Dataset Create a versioned golden dataset with four strata: | Stratum | Purpose | Required ground truth | | --- | --- | --- | | Exact code lookup | Literal identifiers, config keys, errors, paths | exact files, symbols, and spans | | Structural Hook discovery | Hook targets, overloads, callers, annotations | accepted Hook method identity and supporting API/source spans | | Vague semantic intent | Behavior described without repository terminology | accepted implementation area, Hooks, and relevant source evidence | | Community/history dependent | Decisions or failure hints found in curated discussions/releases | relevant note IDs plus the current source/API evidence that verifies or rejects each claim | Each case records: - stable case ID and dataset version; - repository/worktree revision; - natural-language request; - expected source type; - relevant files, symbols, source spans, and Hook identity where applicable; - forbidden or known-wrong files/Hooks; - whether community/history evidence is required; - expected readiness outcome; - task-level acceptance rule. Initial development runs may use controlled fixtures. Interview-grade claims require a separately reported set of real repository tasks that was not used to tune routing rules. ## 4. Formal Experimental Arms | Arm | Retrieval behavior | Role | | --- | --- | --- | | A | `rg` plus live file reads | required baseline | | B | `rg` plus symbol/AST navigation and live revalidation | deterministic structural path | | C | code BM25 only | diagnostic arm, not a proposed authority path | | D | community/history BM25 plus code `rg`/symbol, separated by source authority | source-aware mixed path | | E | B or D plus dense auxiliary retrieval | semantic-recall test | | F | fixed score fusion/RRF over available retrievers | fusion comparison | | G | Agent selects tools, rewrites/retries, and revalidates live code within a fixed budget | Agentic routing comparison | Every arm uses the same dataset split, top-K values, repository revision, readiness policy, proposal/review implementation, and task acceptance rules. Report comparison has three explicit modes: `calibration` produces only `calibration_complete`; `benchmark_measurement` requires fresh benchmark evidence; `promotion` additionally requires the same passing quality policy. For every compared metric, the exact `applicable_case_ids` must match. ### Deferred measurement contracts (not hidden evaluator repairs) - H2/H3 require a unified ranked Hook-result object carrying rank, identity, source span, and live-revalidation provenance. The current parallel `retrieved_hook_ids` representation may support calibration but cannot close H2/H3. - H4 requires an end-to-end modification outcome with wrong-file and no-modification states modeled separately. A single retrieval metric cannot establish the H4 claim. - H5 requires a retry trace with attempt budgets, rewritten queries, evidence transitions, and final task outcome. It is not inferred from aggregate retrieval rows. - The first real Arm A deliverable includes an actual RunManifest collector; caller-authored identity strings are not benchmark evidence. ## 5. Conditional Preregistered Hypotheses H1-H5 ### H1: Historical/Community BM25 Adds Relevant Recall On community/history-dependent cases, Arm D improves Recall@10 by at least 10 percentage points over Arm A while community evidence remains planning-only and does not increase wrong-target decisions by more than 1 percentage point. Decision: - pass: keep persistent BM25 for curated historical/community sources; - fail: do not build a broad community ingestion path until query/data quality is improved and re-evaluated. ### H2: Structural Retrieval Improves Hook Discovery On structural Hook cases, Arm B improves correct Hook Recall@5 by at least 10 percentage points over Arm A, with every consumed result passing live file/hash and method-identity validation. Decision: - pass: keep disposable symbol/AST navigation in the production path; - fail: use `rg` plus live reads as the default and restrict structural indexes to diagnostic use. ### H3: Dense Retrieval Finds Additional Correct Hooks On vague-intent cases, Arm E finds at least 5 percentage points of additional correct Hook Recall@10 beyond the strongest deterministic arm, without reducing correct-file Precision@10 by more than 2 percentage points. Decision: - pass: retain dense retrieval as an auxiliary, never sole patch authority; - fail: defer production dense storage, embedding refresh, and reranking work. ### H4: Source-Aware Routing Reduces Wrong-File Modifications Compared with fixed score fusion, source-aware separation and live-code verification reduce wrong-file modification rate by at least 30 percent relative while final task success is no worse by more than 2 percentage points. Decision: - pass: make source-specific routing and authority conflict resolution the production mixed-retrieval design; - fail: retain deterministic code retrieval and investigate the failed routing or ground-truth assumptions before expanding fusion. ### H5: Agentic Retry Improves Final Success Within Budget On cases where the first retrieval attempt is insufficient, Arm G improves final task success by at least 10 percentage points over the strongest fixed arm, with at most two retrieval retries, median end-to-end latency no more than 2x the fixed arm, and all API/token/monetary costs reported. Decision: - pass: enable bounded Agentic rewrite/retry for classified failure modes; - fail: retain deterministic routing and expose insufficient evidence instead of adding uncontrolled retries. ## 6. Formal Metrics ### Retrieval Metrics - Recall@1, Recall@5, Recall@10; - Precision@5 and Precision@10; - Mean Reciprocal Rank for the first correct Hook/source span; - unique correct Hooks added by each arm; - citation file/symbol/span accuracy; - stale-result rate; - source-authority classification accuracy; - evidence-readiness false-continue and false-block rates. ### Downstream Agent Metrics - correct Hook selection rate; - correct target-file selection rate; - wrong-file modification rate; - unsupported change-unit rate; - proposal-review blocker precision and recall; - first-pass and final controlled-task success; - retrieval retry recovery rate; - repair-loop success and retry exhaustion rate. ### Cost And Performance Metrics - retrieval latency p50/p95; - end-to-end task latency p50/p95; - index build and incremental refresh time; - peak index size and memory use; - model/API call count; - input/output token count; - embedding count and cache-hit rate; - monetary cost per case and per successful task. ## 7. Formal Freshness And Mutation Tests Run every code-index arm through controlled mutations: 1. edit a method body without renaming it; 2. rename a file; 3. rename a symbol; 4. delete a file; 5. switch branch/worktree namespace; 6. change files concurrently between retrieval and EvidencePack consumption; 7. return an intentionally stale index result. The evaluator records: - whether the index refreshes automatically; - whether stale evidence is detected before proposal generation; - whether the system falls back to `rg` and live reads; - whether a stale result can reach readiness, proposal, or review; - refresh and fallback latency. No code-index strategy passes production validation if stale evidence can grant patch authority. ## 8. Experiment Execution Order Implementation status on 2026-07-11: - `V2-EVAL-001-FOLLOWUP` is complete at the evaluator-contract boundary after focused verification. Policy recomputation, explicit comparison modes and applicable populations, external-evaluation graph authority, strict inputs, and split observation hashes are implemented. Actual identity collection is deliberately the first Arm A capability, not a caller-authored evaluator field. - `V2-RET-001A-SMOKE-ARTIFACT` retained internally consistent v1/v2 artifacts; v2 supports an engineering-level harness-run conclusion but does not itself attest binary identity or exact searchable-corpus equivalence. - `V2-RET-001A-AUTHENTICITY` is complete with formal smoke v5. The formal runner owns provider/collector construction; exact rg executable identity, argv, normalized environment and command traces are recorded; rg searches only the canonical snapshot file list; returned files are rehashed; the exclusive result ledger hashes persisted bytes. The smoke is explicitly non-promotion and its tuned cases are excluded from held-out reuse. - Formal v5 values are measured smoke observations, not held-out Arm A quality results. No BM25, dense, fusion, Agentic-routing, or H1-H5 result exists. 1. `GTFO-VSLICE-001C` completed: the deterministic downstream consumer and repair-decision taxonomy are stable for the registered evaluation path. 2. `V2-EVAL-001-FOLLOWUP` completed at the evaluator-contract boundary. 3. `V2-RET-001A-AUTHENTICITY` completed as non-promotion execution-plumbing evidence; it is not a retrieval-direction result. 4. Completed: `V2-RET-DIRECTIONAL-001` saved frozen A/B/D raw evidence and a bounded decision report. The result retains A (`rg` plus live reads), defers SymbolIndexer deepening until repeated structural-navigation failures, and defers community BM25 until authentic traceable material exists. Product delivery resumes with `V2-CODEGEN-REAL-001`. 5. Keep the formal held-out Arm A design already produced as future material; do not let it block the directional pilot or current product work. 6. Trigger only the relevant formal `V2-RET-001A/B/C` measurement when a later product decision requires an H1-H5 or promotion-grade claim. 7. Project a selected production path into dashboard/MCP surfaces only when the product path itself needs those surfaces, not merely to display an experiment. ## 9. Formal Required Outputs Each formal benchmark run produces: - immutable experiment configuration; - dataset and repository revision; - per-case retrieval results and evidence refs; - per-arm metric summary; - latency and cost summary; - stale-index mutation results; - failures and excluded cases with reasons; - hypothesis verdicts; - production-path decision and rollback condition. Results must distinguish fixture-only, local-repository, and real-world task evidence. A passing fixture benchmark alone is not a production claim. ## 10. Formal Stopping Rules - Stop dense expansion when H3 fails; do not compensate by adding reranking or more infrastructure before diagnosing recall and ground truth. - Stop Agentic retry when the retry budget is exhausted or evidence remains insufficient. - Stop any arm that allows stale or non-authoritative evidence to approve a target file or Hook. - Do not promote an arm on retrieval metrics alone when downstream wrong-file or task-success metrics regress beyond the preregistered bounds.

documents.title: V2 Mainline Transition
documents.text: # V2 Mainline Transition [PROPOSED] This document is a non-normative transition draft. It does not define V2 completion criteria, create a product gate, impose an implementation requirement, select a product direction, or change the implementation queue. ## Status labels [PROPOSED] Each substantive statement in this draft uses exactly one of these labels: - [OBSERVED] Directly recorded by the preserved real-run EvidencePack or trace. - [SOURCE_CONFIRMED] Confirmed by current registered source inspected for the stated claim. - [INFERRED] A bounded interpretation of recorded evidence. - [UNKNOWN] Not established by the evidence currently cited here. - [PROPOSED] A reviewable idea with no normative or queue effect. [OBSERVED] Current registered source was not inspected during this document migration, so this draft contains no SOURCE_CONFIRMED transition claim. [OBSERVED] Later runtime-path reconstruction, component-responsibility mapping, Phase 1 lineage validation, and Phase 2A delivery-canary work occurred after the initial migration text above. The later proposed target and the observed migration checkpoints are preserved below without upgrading this document to normative authority. ## Preserved V2-C evidence boundary - [OBSERVED] One repaired-path real run completed the bounded intelligent loop with capability=true and semantic=true. - [OBSERVED] The same run recorded convergence=false, readiness=partial, and can_generate_patch=false. - [OBSERVED] The run did not bind source_revision, git_commit, or modified_files_hash; its recorded status is source_binding_status=missing. - [OBSERVED] The run produced no Proposal, Patch, Build, or runtime artifact. - [INFERRED] This evidence supports freezing V2-C as a validation spike, but it does not establish a continuing V2-C product route. ## Runtime-path questions - [UNKNOWN] Which current entry point initiates the relevant Agent execution. - [UNKNOWN] Which current path carries intelligent decisions during a real run. - [UNKNOWN] Which persisted artifacts and trace records are sufficient to reconstruct one run from entry to terminal observation. - [UNKNOWN] Whether more than one current path performs overlapping roles. - [UNKNOWN] Where evidence continuity first becomes unavailable if the path cannot be reconstructed end to end. ## State and control questions - [UNKNOWN] Where the relevant runtime state is created, updated, persisted, and consumed in current source. - [UNKNOWN] Which current component performs retry, stop, and terminal routing in the observed path. - [UNKNOWN] Whether the recorded V2-C loop shares those responsibilities or is isolated experimental scaffolding. - [INFERRED] Resolving these questions may clarify whether existing paths can be described consistently without introducing a new state model. ## Reviewable runtime-path shapes - [PROPOSED] Shape A: document the existing graph-centred path if source and trace show that one graph already carries entry, routing, and terminal state. - [PROPOSED] Shape B: document an existing admission facade feeding the graph if source and trace show a stable pre-graph control boundary. - [PROPOSED] Shape C: document separate control, intelligent-execution, and evidence paths if source shows that no single current path owns all three. - [PROPOSED] None of these shapes is selected, canonical, required, or a reason to create implementation work. ## Later proposed V2 target architecture [PROPOSED] The review direction developed after the initial runtime-path shapes is the following responsibility flow. It is a target shape for evaluating incremental migration, not a declaration that every box exists as a separate module or service: ```text [PROPOSED] User / Product Request | v [PROPOSED] Thin Admission / Lifecycle Boundary | v [PROPOSED] LangGraph Runtime Core | v [PROPOSED] Intelligence Components | v [PROPOSED] Verification Layer ``` ### Thin Admission / Lifecycle Boundary - [PROPOSED] Accept the concrete user or product request. - [PROPOSED] Bind the approved source, worktree, Source Registry identity, and source revision or snapshot identity before execution. - [PROPOSED] Create or bind run identity and preserve one lineage across the selected execution. - [PROPOSED] Record authorization and external-disclosure boundaries before the affected action occurs. - [PROPOSED] Bind the terminal record to the same request, source, authorization, run, and produced Artifact lineage. - [PROPOSED] Do not own graph-internal routing, intelligence decisions, or node retry/repair decisions. - [PROPOSED] Do not replace the LangGraph runtime or imply a separately deployed Lifecycle Service. ### LangGraph Runtime Core - [PROPOSED] Reuse the existing LangGraph StateGraph as the single runtime orchestration core. - [PROPOSED] Keep node orchestration, conditional routing, runtime state transitions, retry/repair routing, and applicable runtime verification gates inside that control plane. - [PROPOSED] Do not make the graph responsible for an external product-lifecycle service, multi-user task administration, or a general scheduling platform. ### Intelligence Components - [PROPOSED] Keep planning, evidence discovery, retrieval, implementation planning, Proposal generation, patch generation, and build planning as bounded capabilities used by the runtime. - [PROPOSED] Intelligence components provide structured outputs and evidence; they do not independently authorize writes or select the final graph route. - [PROPOSED] Reuse existing components before adding another orchestration or execution framework. ### Verification Layer - [PROPOSED] Runtime verification supplies facts that may affect the current continue, block, repair, or terminal route when the selected request requires that verification. - [PROPOSED] Post-run validation audits claims such as capability, semantic, convergence, and readiness without silently becoming graph-route authority. - [PROPOSED] Persist verification results with the same source-bound run lineage and state whether each result affected runtime routing. - [PROPOSED] Do not treat post-run evaluation alone as proof of product behavior or as a replacement for build or runtime evidence. ## Proposed migration strategy [PROPOSED] The current migration path reuses existing implementation and adds only the minimum boundary exposed by a real vertical slice: ```text [PROPOSED] Thin Admission Boundary | v [PROPOSED] Existing LangGraph Runtime | v [PROPOSED] Existing Intelligence Components | v [PROPOSED] Runtime / Post-run Verification | v [PROPOSED] Terminal Record ``` [PROPOSED] Do not implement a complete Lifecycle Service merely to match the target diagram. A separate Lifecycle Service and Runtime Worker boundary may be reviewed only if real product requirements introduce multi-user operation, asynchronous execution, a remote API product, or long-running task management. [PROPOSED] If one of those triggers is established, the later shape to review is: ```text [PROPOSED] Lifecycle Service | v [PROPOSED] Runtime Workers using the controlled LangGraph runtime ``` [PROPOSED] Such a later review does not automatically authorize a service, scheduler, database, worker fleet, or migration task. ## Proposed migration constraints 1. [PROPOSED] Do not create a second workflow or orchestration engine. 2. [PROPOSED] Do not let Admission directly control graph-internal routing. 3. [PROPOSED] Do not let Lifecycle state replace LangGraph runtime state. 4. [PROPOSED] Do not make ArtifactStore state, evaluator state, or graph state individually authoritative for every kind of state; retain their bounded responsibilities and explicit lineage links. 5. [PROPOSED] Do not design a new unified RunState without an observed failure and direct current-source evidence that existing state cannot represent the required lineage. 6. [PROPOSED] Do not build a complete task scheduling, multi-tenant, or remote execution platform before a real product requirement establishes the need. [PROPOSED] These constraints prevent migration drift. They do not define V2 completion criteria, activate implementation, or prevent a later reviewed architecture decision based on new evidence. ## Minimal unresolved migration questions - [UNKNOWN] Whether all current product entry points should converge on one thin boundary or retain several entry-specific adapters behind one contract. - [UNKNOWN] Which exact persisted identity should be the common run-lineage key across entry, graph execution, Artifact revisions, verification, and terminal closure for future product slices. - [UNKNOWN] How every supported source type should bind repository revision, worktree or snapshot identity, registry identity, and permitted file scope. - [UNKNOWN] Which terminal outcomes require runtime verification, post-run validation, both, or an explicit not-applicable record for each product request. - [UNKNOWN] Whether evaluator verdict persistence needs any boundary beyond the existing ArtifactStore and terminal-record contracts. [PROPOSED] Resolve only the first unknown that blocks a selected real product slice. Do not expand this list into a microservice, database, scheduler, or multi-tenant platform design. ## Migration phases and observed checkpoints ### Phase 1: Runtime Boundary Stabilization [PROPOSED] Validate that one source-bound no-write request can travel through: ```text [PROPOSED] Request -> Thin Admission Boundary -> LangGraph Runtime -> Intelligence Component -> Runtime / Post-run Verification -> Terminal Record ``` [OBSERVED] `V2-RUNTIME-BOUNDARY-001` completed this bounded validation for the registered `gtfo-r8-modules-asm` source. Run `intelligent_evidence_4c811b6933d54a258b8ba0b2c4e14229` persisted source and run identity, workflow trace, post-run validation, and terminal attempt lineage without Proposal, apply, build, runtime, or target-source-write artifacts. ### Phase 2: Product delivery slices [PROPOSED] Select a real Mod request and exercise the required controlled chain through planning, evidence, implementation plan, Proposal, review, dry-run, approval, isolated apply, build, applicable verification, and truthful terminal classification. [OBSERVED] Phase 2A run `42c5d93c` completed only the source-bound delivery pipeline canary for the BetterHitFeedback VERSION change. It established `delivery_canary_complete=true`, while `product_slice_complete=false`, `runtime_behavior_verified=false`, and `phase_2_complete=false` remain explicit. [PROPOSED] Phase 2B selects a meaningful product behavior or maintenance slice whose acceptance boundary demonstrates more than pipeline mechanics. [OBSERVED] `PHASE2B-BETTERHITFEEDBACK-ENABLED-001` later selected the meaningful BetterHitFeedback `General.Enabled` startup-registration behavior slice. Controlled run `007b1b58` bound one source and run lineage through Evidence, Implementation Plan, Proposal, deterministic review, no-write dry-run, exact diff approval, isolated apply, and real build. The exact final DLL then passed separate real GTFO `Enabled=false` and `Enabled=true` checks: the disabled mode returned before patch registration, while the enabled mode registered patches and produced bound gameplay Hook and behavior markers. The original game directory state was restored after capture. This satisfies the proposed Phase 2B checkpoint for this selected slice; it does not turn every product-delivery case into a verified capability or activate optional Phase 3. ### Phase 3: Optional Lifecycle Evolution [PROPOSED] Review a separate Lifecycle Service only after real product demand demonstrates multi-user, asynchronous, remote-API, or long-running task management requirements that the thin boundary and existing runtime cannot represent safely. [PROPOSED] Phase 3 is optional, inactive, and not implied by completion of Phase 1, Phase 2A, or any future Phase 2B slice. ## Productization topics for later review - [PROPOSED] Review source binding, entry visibility, trace continuity, retry behavior, stop behavior, terminal reporting, and path isolation as separate topics rather than as a bundled specification. - [PROPOSED] Compare any later product direction using user-visible outcome, contract relevance, available evidence, minimal vertical observability, source reachability, dependencies, unknowns, and implementation risk. - [PROPOSED] Keep grounded/walkable behavior, collision/contact response, and other gameplay directions unselected unless a later human decision selects one. ## Abstention and stop conditions for this analysis - [PROPOSED] Abstain from describing a runtime path when the exact registered source or a readable trace/EvidencePack is unavailable. - [PROPOSED] Stop at the first explicit evidence break and record the missing material instead of inferring a Hook, owner, or mechanism. - [PROPOSED] Do not convert an inferred path into a source-confirmed statement without direct current-source evidence. - [PROPOSED] Do not create a task id, queue item, product gate, implementation requirement, or product-direction decision from this draft.

documents.title: Agent instruction and workflow maintenance — 2026-09-23
documents.text: # Agent instruction and workflow maintenance — 2026-09-23 Status: bounded implementation and independent review complete. One workflow checkpoint assertion remains failed, as recorded below. ## Overall assessment and boundary The observed problems are stale instructions, overly broad skill triggers, mechanical verification requirements and duplicated implementation with divergent behavior. They are not evidence that fewer rules always improve a model, or that the product's binding and execution checks should be weakened. This change targets repository instructions, the five active repository skills, their direct helpers, the existing workflow and the explicitly added `src/mod_agent/local_entry.py`. External lookups are limited to exact references needed to decide whether a listed symbol has callers. Frozen playbooks are not loaded or restored. Existing WIP, original model runs, permissions, budgets and product artifacts are not reset or relabeled as successful. The official guidance used is: - [Rethinking skills and prompts for GPT-6 Astra](https://developers.openai.com/blog/rethinking-skills-and-prompts-for-gpt-6-astra): narrow skill descriptions, progressive disclosure, contextual reading, and reconsideration of old scaffolding. - [GPT-6 testing and verification guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model#testing-and-verification): meaningful checks proportional to the change, with broader or repeated checks justified by new changes, failures or unresolved concerns. | Guidance actually used | Application here | Limit of the inference | |---|---|---| | Short, discriminating skill descriptions | Ordinary test requests must not select an all-system QA itinerary. | Shortness alone does not establish correct skill selection. | | Progressive disclosure and contextual repository reading | Keep references discoverable and read the relevant mode; remove a mandatory cognition/document prelude. | Concrete callers and fragile contracts still need inspection. | | Reconsider elaborate recipes written for older models | Remove fixed retry counts, fabricated résumé metrics and mandatory boilerplate resources. | Deterministic identity, persistence and permission checks remain necessary where code depends on them. | | Define completion and avoid unnecessary approval pauses | Continue authorized maintenance through its declared verification; distinguish recoverable feedback from executor defects. | This does not authorize new model disclosure, product Apply or game operations. | | Proportionate testing | Use state-loss, write-failure and helper-input counterexamples plus affected callers. | Test success is neither product acceptance nor a measured Astra performance gain. | The requirement to give each retained rule a reason, inspect conflicts against actual code and obtain a separate review comes from the user's request. The current bundled `C:/Users/10160/.codex/skills/.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md` was also consulted for scoped triggers, optional resources and behavioral validation; it is local tooling guidance, not a performance benchmark. These sources inform instruction design, not correctness of this repository's implementation. Local source, counterexamples and review provide that evidence. No new product-model, Build, game, training or Cloud acceptance is part of this maintenance. No Astra throughput or task-success improvement is measured here. ## Retained rules and falsifiable reasons | Root rule | Concrete reason and code/contract boundary | What would contradict the reason | |---|---|---| | 1: scope and completion | Audit, platform maintenance and product execution have different requested outcomes. `run_local_request` is an execution entry, not an instruction to run it. | A read-only request starting a model run, or an implementation stopping with analysis only. | | 2: WIP and history | `local_entry.py` already contained the gap/query/budget work before cleanup. Historical `run_result.json` is used to interpret the original attempt. | Removal of inherited hunks or changes to a historical attempt to match new code. | | 3: bounded source reading and large-file plan | Public entry, graph assembly and checkpoint handling span large files with different responsibilities. | A split changing public behavior without call-site evidence, or repository-wide reading without a task need. | | 4: contextual references | The contract's opening selection was stale while historical and current facts coexisted below it. A static ownership map describes responsibility rather than enforcing it. | Treating a documentation paragraph or query view as current runtime proof or execution permission. | | 5: inactive materials | The old task packet selected a Fresh-only objective and an old base commit; hooks have a fixed active packet path. | A restored old packet overriding the current user request. Old snapshots remain history and must still be treated as non-authoritative. | | 6: existing control and persistence | Workflow conditional edges and ArtifactStore are existing consumer boundaries. Checkpoint and operation return types have callers. | A helper extraction creating a second routing authority or changing serialized return contracts. | | 7: roles are not permissions | `StateOwnershipPolicy` declares writers; it is not itself a runtime source-edit authorization mechanism. Model suggestions are validated by execution owners. | Documentation claiming that a declaration or retrieved path itself permits mutation. | | 8: exact operation scope | Product Apply, model disclosure and runtime execution carry bound identities and explicit admission. Platform repository maintenance is a different action. | Reusing approval for changed bytes/scope, bypassing denial, or requiring a product Apply token for a requested local code edit. | | 9: task-memory limits | Stored observations can support planning; they do not establish that current dependencies and source still match. | A retrieved lesson selecting writable paths or turning an untested diagnosis into fact. | | 10: proportional checks | State copying and failed writes have behavior counterexamples; documentation size has none of those runtime side effects. | Treating repeated broad test counts as new evidence, or omitting direct-call regressions after behavior changes. | | 11: recoverable feedback vs executor failure | The product has a bounded feedback loop, and failures must retain their original inputs and consumed budget. | Stopping every supported feedback action as a new engineering failure, or repeatedly running an unchanged broken executor. | | 12: claim boundaries and independent review | Build, dry-run and observed behavior prove different results. A reviewer who did not author the patch can challenge assumptions. | Calling a preview an execution, AI review human verification, or peer review a guarantee of correctness. | | 13: one detailed record and scoped skills | Duplicate status text and broad triggers made obsolete instructions appear current. | Multiple competing verification accounts or skills forcing unrelated work. | The reasons above are hypotheses about useful constraints, not self-issued certificates. The review and verification sections below must record contrary evidence and unresolved limitations as well as passes. ## Disposition of the earlier A/B/C findings Findings that change behavior are not presented as cosmetic cleanup. The workflow and skill rows below have implementation, direct checks and independent review evidence; unresolved retirement and checkpoint items remain explicit. | Finding group | Intended treatment | Acceptance / reason to retain | |---|---|---| | A1/A2/A6: obsolete paths, QA inputs and tool names | Implemented: corrected helper paths; removed mandatory absent-plan and unavailable-question-tool assumptions. | Helpers resolve the real repository; explicitly supplied missing inputs fail clearly. | | A3/A4: QA execution itinerary | Implemented: removed all-tests, serial one-row edits, fixed retry counts and wording-driven reruns. | QA scope follows the request; helper mutation and provider scope remain explicit. Valid evidence reuse does not force another run. | | A5: unsupported résumé claims | Implemented: removed suggested achievements, numerical ranges and stale ready-to-use accomplishments. | Claims require observed results and contribution evidence; code presence does not establish personal authorship. | | A7: root rule duplication | Implemented: 291 lines became 100, with 13 scoped rules and reasons. | Separate review found no lost required boundary; this is not evidence of improved model throughput. | | A8: stale active task packet | Implemented: archived with identical bytes and verified hash. | The active path is absent; previously recorded snapshots remain historical. | | A9: stale graph documentation | Implemented: distinguish default no-write fake path from injected exact dry-run adapter. | No execution path or permission changed to match prose. | | B1: state-copy divergence | Implemented: shared runtime cloning; retained separate historical checkpoint projection. | The dropped review field now survives with an independent nested copy; checkpoint format is unchanged. | | B2: resume consumption ordering | Implemented: consume only after a durable/committed report. | Old write-failure counterexample fails; fixed same-instance retry passes. | | B3: Runtime preflight duplication | Implemented and independently reviewed: common facts, separate mode rules and failure codes. | Extra-upstream counterexample still distinguishes terminal and consolidation. | | B4/B5/C8: possible dead code | Removed `is_vague_request`, `continue_route` and `_MaterializedRepairPatchLLM`, each unreferenced in the checked scope. Production-called helpers retained; tests-only islands remain retirement-unverified. | A test import is not proof of production need. Exact classification is below; external consumers were not audited. | | C1–C7: helper defects | Implemented: correct roots, explicit isolated QA targets and path checks; bound/sealed backups; failure propagation; structural-only note lint; nonempty skill metadata and real YAML parsing; optional scaffold resources; archive exclusion of itself/cache/temp; no credential-prefix logging. | Disposable-file counterexamples pass. The helper guards are not an operating-system sandbox or protection against arbitrary concurrent hostile mutation. | | C9–C11: local-entry duplication | Implemented: remove unused local bindings, share legacy Build/XML value parsing. | Typed/legacy Build checks and optional/required XML error behavior passed their focused checks. | | Fixed release/handoff schemas | Keep current CLI/output contracts; narrow skill descriptions to supported tasks. | Removing prose alone cannot make an unsupported input valid. Generalizing schemas is not required for this cleanup. | Correction to the first audit: the QA helper source contains destructive and provider-switch operations, but its current root calculation points at `.agents`. That does not establish that it actually cleared the real production store. Repairing the root must not accidentally make those operations implicit defaults. ### What was retained, and what the evidence does not establish - `_patch_generation_obligation_projection`, `_validated_plan_change_identity_and_validation` and `_overlay_generated_patch_changes_on_plan` have production callers in `LocalOllamaInitialPatchAdapter`; they are not part of the unused repair island. - `_repair_history_fact_constraints`, `_unique_repair_diagnostics`, `_repair_provider_constraints`, `_runtime_source_diagnostic_lines`, `_runtime_repair_spans`, `_objective_verification_source_views`, `_repair_span_response_schema`, `_materialize_repair_span_change`, `_repair_review_context` and `_read_utf8_source_snapshot` have direct tests in `tests/unit/test_local_entry.py`, but no production caller was found in the checked scope. `_RuntimeRepairSpan` and `_implementation_with_runtime_repair_bindings` belong to that island. They are **retirement-unverified**, not proven necessary production code. They remain to avoid silently deleting a tested historical interface while its replacement/retirement boundary is unverified; their existing tests cannot themselves settle that retirement decision. - `StubNodeRunner` is used by the graph's blocked path and is exported. `StateOwnershipPolicy` is exported and read as declarations by `scripts/engineering_cognition.py`; its executable method use found here is in `test_mod_agent_state.py`, not a production write gate. It is retained as a declaration/compatibility surface, without adding new enforcement. - Ollama wrappers translate exceptions at the local entry boundary; the checkpoint snapshot has an existing persisted-format contract. Similar-looking implementations are not removed when that would erase their distinct boundary. The dead-symbol lookup was bounded to exact names in `src`, `scripts` and `tests` Python files. It does not establish the absence of unknown external imports. No tests were deleted to manufacture a passing cleanup result. ## Split plans for files exceeding 800 lines Counts below are the pre-change structural inventory. Plans do not authorize a wholesale migration. Small helper extractions for the listed findings are allowed; public imports, serialized contracts and historical artifacts remain compatible. | File | Lines | Proposed responsibility split | Why this boundary | |---|---:|---|---| | `src/mod_agent/local_entry.py` | 14562 | Public request façade; model/Patch adapter; query/budget assembly; approved/frozen continuation; Build; separate Runtime admission, execution and terminal-result helpers. | These operations have different side effects and validation identities; moving all Runtime code into another giant file would not help. | | `src/mod_agent/workflow/graph.py` | 6425 | Keep `build_graph`; extract control validation, node registration, edge registration, stage implementations and Trace helpers. | The graph must remain one control plane with the original callable entry. | | `src/mod_agent/workflow/checkpointing.py` | 2282 | Keep public data types and store façade; separate persistence, resume fact loading, Runtime-specific preflight and lineage checks. | Shared validation must not erase terminal/consolidation differences or change historical payload formats. | | `.agents/skills/release-evidence-packager/scripts/package_release_evidence.py` | 822 | Input validation; evidence projection; Markdown rendering; atomic file output; thin CLI. | These existing responsibilities can be reviewed separately without changing the current output schema. | | `docs/ACTIVE_PRODUCT_CONTRACT.md` | 1762 | Short current selection; stable execution boundary; links to preserved historical records. | The opening state must not present a historical 3/11 run as current. Historical paragraphs are labeled now; full relocation needs link-preserving review. | | `tests/unit/test_workflow_graph.py` | 8096 | Group node behavior, routing, approval, recovery and runtime verification tests. | Preserve fixture sharing and test collection identities; do not delete coverage to shorten a file. | | `tests/unit/test_local_entry.py` | 4869 | Group admission, model/Patch adapter, Build, Runtime and terminal-result checks. | Separate independent execution surfaces while retaining their error and compatibility assertions. | ## Verification and independent review Workflow and skill implementation and independent review are complete. Commands below use the repository's `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -B -m pytest`, run from the repository root. | Check | Result and boundary | |---|---| | State-copy and failed-report-write counterexamples | Old code: 2 failed. Fixed code: 2 passed. The tests now live in `tests/unit/test_workflow_cleanup.py`; the old locations were in `test_workflow_graph.py` and `test_verification_only_continuation.py`. | | `test_verification_operation_checkpointing.py` plus exact resume/result, terminal-preflight and consolidation-owner tests | 23 passed. Checks persisted/committed resume handling and operation-specific admission. | | Cleanup tests plus public Build admission/order and XML property tests | 7 passed. No real Build was performed. | | Cleanup tests plus `test_seven_shape_public_operation_matrix_uses_exact_typed_chain` | 11 passed. Covers typed/legacy operation compatibility. | | Final two terminal/consolidation focused checks after the last helper edit | 2 passed. | | Bounded two-worker checkpoint: `test_workflow_cleanup.py test_mod_agent_state.py test_verification_operation_checkpointing.py test_repair_checkpoint_smoke.py test_workflow_route_trace.py -q --tb=short -n 2 --dist=loadfile` | **37 passed, 1 failed.** The failure is not hidden or counted as passed. | | Exact failure rerun: `test_repair_checkpoint_smoke.py::test_repair_review_checkpoint_resume_accepts_review_approval` | The same assertion fails serially: line 53, `proposal_review.allowed_next_stage` is `None`, expected `dry_run_apply`. | For that remaining failure, a separate Python process replaced only the reachable `WorkflowCheckpointStore.resume` implementation with its exact old consumption- before-write version and ran the same test: **1 failed with the same signature**. The review result is constructed by `ProposalReviewer` in `_repair_review_state` before checkpoint/resume operations. This supports that the observed failure is not removed by restoring the changed resume logic; it is not a whole-repository baseline reconstruction. Its cause is not diagnosed or fixed in this cleanup. A separate AI reviewer, who did not implement these patches, ran the four cleanup tests (4 passed), reviewed the diff and constructed an in-memory RuntimeEvidence with an extra `evidence_pack` upstream. Terminal continuation rejected it with `RUNTIME_TERMINAL_EVIDENCE_LINEAGE_INVALID`; consolidation accepted it. This counterexample confirms that extraction preserved their different upstream requirements. Freshness and outer lineage dependencies were fixed test doubles; it is not real Runtime evidence. The inline check wrote no files. The reviewer independently found that a backup restore still overwrote a later configuration change: the three skill-test files initially reported **33 passed, 1 failed** at `test_restore_rejects_unsealed_target_drift`. The helper now records the restorable target state and its own writes update that state; third-party drift rejects restoration. The exact drift/owned-write pair passed (2 passed), then the final bounded checkpoint passed: ```text .venv/Scripts/python.exe -B -m pytest tests/unit/test_project_skill_maintenance.py tests/unit/test_project_skill_safety.py tests/unit/test_project_skill_scripts.py -q --tb=short -n 2 --dist=loadfile 35 passed ``` The independent reviewer repeated these 35 checks successfully after the fix. This also covers a prepared QA baseline reporting failure when required fixture or command steps fail, rather than returning a success message and exit code. No actual ingestion, provider switch, remote request or active-store deletion was performed. The original `test_project_skill_scripts.py` has no content diff; new cases live in two small files. The filesystem checks exercised resolution/containment logic, including a monkeypatched external-path counterexample. A real Windows junction was not created in this verification. Review covered this cleanup's hunks, not all inherited `local_entry.py` work. No unresolved high/medium-priority finding was reported within that reviewed scope; this is not a claim of defect absence. Changed workflow/entry files and changed skill helpers/tests passed Ruff's `--select E9,F63,F7` checks. `git diff --check` passed for the touched tracked files; line-ending conversion notices are not test failures. The reviewer also caught a missing evidence link in the current contract header. That header now links the retained local `run_result.json` and `run_manifest.json` directly rather than using this maintenance report as proof. This is independent source review and local behavioral verification, not a blind model evaluation, human certification, a full-suite pass or an Astra performance measurement. CI itself has not been executed by this maintenance. `local_entry.py` and workflow source identities changed in this maintenance. Any later real continuation must load the current version and regenerate its bound Preview before execution; this report neither updates an old scope hash nor renews its approval. The retained run history and cumulative budget remain unchanged. The existing CI selection now includes the new focused cleanup and skill-helper test files, without adding a new workflow or running live services. ### Visible compatibility changes and approval outcome - The QA state helpers now require `--target-repo` and a marked independent checkout; the previous implicit-target invocations are intentionally rejected. This prevents correcting the root path from silently enabling active-store mutation. The marker does not establish operating-system isolation. - `qa_validate_notes.py` takes an explicit progress file and reports structural validity only. It does not enforce particular evidence wording or prohibit a valid reference to another version-bound result. - `init_skill.py` creates only `SKILL.md` by default. `--include-examples` retains the former resource examples when requested. The initializer is not represented as creating UI metadata that its implementation does not write. - Bounded handoff and release helper input/output contracts were preserved. Their remaining fixed restrictions are compatibility limits, not claims that those restrictions are best practice for all tasks. Automatic approval review rejected an attempted delete-then-add edit of the QA `SKILL.md` and `references/test_patterns.md`, because it interpreted the operation as removing an active skill without a replacement. That deletion did not occur. The cleanup was written as in-place updates; the user then explicitly approved both files. They remain present (71 and 51 lines respectively), and this approval is not extended to unrelated actions. ## Archived active context The old ignored task packet was moved from `.codex/task-packet.json` to `.codex/task-packet.retired-20260923.json`. Its bytes are unchanged; SHA-256 is `2174d15c22894b489c0399403cadf8aa7bf00a3f436534f748b3789a900a4e09`. This is an inactive context archive, not a new task registry or run result. ## Follow-up performance pilot and return to product work The user subsequently authorized measuring instruction-cleanup benefits. This is a separate follow-up, not a retroactive change to the cleanup verification. The tested intervention was old/new repository instruction Markdown with the same helper code, three disposable diagnostic tasks, GPT-6 Astra / High, Codex CLI 0.155.0-alpha.9.2, separate workspaces and 240 seconds per run. It did not test the product Qwen model, RAG runtime or real Mod delivery. The diagnostic tasks were authored by Codex and reviewed by a separate AI agent; they are not human-authored held-out benchmark tasks. The original frozen plan contained 12 runs (two repetitions per arm/task). The user requested rapid closure and return to project progress: runs 01–06 form one old/new pair per task; 07 was cancelled and excluded; 08–12 were not started. The original plan and failed/partial records remain intact; no run was retried or given more time to improve the result. | Diagnostic task | Old instructions | New instructions | CLI input tokens old → new | Command execution batches old → new | CLI wall time old → new | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | T1 nested configuration copy | Complete; behavior and trace review passed | Complete; behavior and trace review passed | 119,043 → 127,013 (+6.7%) | 4 → 6 | 192.4s → 218.3s | | T2 bounded switch-parser QA | Generated code and verification passed; final delivery incomplete at timeout | Complete; behavior and trace review passed | Unavailable → 134,127 | 10 → 8 | 240s timeout → 206.8s complete | | T3 evidence-constrained project description | Complete; semantic review passed | Complete; semantic review passed | 124,956 → 84,982 (−32.0%) | 4 → 4 | 154.5s → 157.9s | All generated behavioral artifacts met the checks reached, but complete deliveries were old 2/3 and new 3/3. The timed-out old T2 has no final turn.completed usage record: unavailable token usage is not zero, and its 240-second timeout is a censored endpoint, not a measured completion time. Do not infer a precise speedup from that row. Cache and output differences matter. T1 uncached input was 15,363 → 12,581, while output was 1,575 → 1,938. T3 uncached input was 23,964 → 22,774, while output was 704 → 906. CLI usage is reported usage, not a provider billing reconciliation; no monetary saving is established. Every scored run logged five WebSocket retries before HTTP fallback. The network wait is part of wall time and prevents treating it as pure model processing time. A separate initial connectivity probe also failed local execution because the test launcher omitted the host's existing windows.sandbox="elevated" setting while ignoring user configuration. The setting was restored for the successful second probe and every scored run. The native workspace sandbox and managed restrictions remained enabled; neither approval rules nor certificate validation were bypassed. Conclusion: mixed diagnostic results, with no established stable speedup, overall cost reduction or general capability improvement. The writing task used fewer reported input tokens; the small code-fix task used more command batches and had higher observed wall time. Maintenance and correctness reasons still justify the cleanup, but this pilot is not a resume performance claim. Raw protocol, invocations, JSONL events, usage, diffs, judgments and blind reviews remain under C:/Users/10160/.codex/visualizations/2026/09/20/01a0bce8-aea4-71d0-8008-83c271251d2f/instruction-perf-20260923/. The result index is results.json / results.csv; pilot-stop.json records the reduction. The original protocol SHA-256 is d0d2ba736ae4f9a46cc806d3d6b81ba7c41082bb35e28ebcaa61297c22726d0c. The user's current priority is product progress with evidence/material collection in parallel, not immediate resume drafting. The original Mod owner has been asked to continue the bounded shortcut task; the integration owner maintains the existing acceptance/material index. Keep the latest real Mod result at 13/17 until a new bound execution actually occurs. Preserve the distinction between historical domain rejection and later stop-record wiring.

documents.title: 项目成果、企业问题与待测证据
documents.text: # 项目成果、企业问题与待测证据 更新于2026-09-30。目标场景包括自然语言新建Mod、生成过程中的迭代修复，以及既有代码库的需求修改与缺陷修复：让生成的代码经过真实验收、在明确范围内应用，并能查清失败及成本。当前为研发原型；企业部署、人工工时节省及业务收益尚无实测数据。 用户职责沿用已提供事实：需求定义、架构与技术选型、验收设计，结合AI编码工具推进实现。Astra的开发工作、产品本地模型结果和独立评测分别归因。为什么要有它：平台里存在某个模块或模型做过某项工作，不能直接成为个人独立完成或产品自主交付的表述。 ## 七项待填均保留，按实际问题取得数据 以下是当前证据索引，原始报告保留版本、分母和评分方式；新运行不改写旧基线。为什么要有它：当前状态需要简短可信，同时能追到真实数字。 同日后续修改fo2从已交付new2源码完成空/空白Message不日志，原worker自动执行5场景/15检查，任务委托Apply与正式Build完成，最终DLL再验通过；父版本两个新增场景反例仍输出日志。新旧源码谱系与原配置分别绑定，父工程未改。成功运行含路由18,437 Token，首次基础设施失败fo1含路由18,445 Token；该开发题独立任务增量0。[派生交付与原失败](../artifacts/eval_driven_20260930/followup_entry/result.json)。 9月30日新增一项自然语言新建开发题：“启动公告”经真实编译错误修订、开发者配置cold Load行为验收、任务委托Apply和正式Build完成交付，最终DLL三种配置场景再验通过。new2为8次产品生成＋1次路由、23,596总Token；此前new1未交付、含路由54,072 Token，两个运行均保留。CS1061反馈实际携带当前依赖XML说明，模型随后修正日志API；这不是独立因果对照或稳定成功率。独立任务增量0，未运行构造器、Chainloader或游戏。[原件、成本与边界](../artifacts/eval_driven_20260930/natural_entry/result.json)。 | 原待测方向 | 企业关心的问题 | 目前可填写的事实及原件 | 下一项证据怎样取得 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 端到端交付 | 维护任务能否从需求走到可用修改，减少多少技术救援？ | 已有AccurateCrosshair配置开发题通过5项检查及Apply/Build；9月30日[br4源码修复复验](../artifacts/eval_driven_20260930/compilation_candidate_product/result.json)在原编译失败输入上也完成该链，5次调用、26,729总Token，属于已暴露夹具、独立任务增量0。独立工程评测仍为同一自有C#工程题集2个变体，冻结基线三轮0/6次、候选1/6次；首轮0/2与1/2另存。[独立重复][E1] | 每个新任务记录真实项目/语言/类型与来源、成功数、人工事件和保留行为；新工程/根因家族验证迁移。重复、同题调优和开发者控制不增加独立任务数。 | | RAG与选型 | 调查是否取得正确依据，避免找错实现或无证据断言？ | 3份RFC、90块、14留出题；BM25/Hybrid必需证据组9/16、8/16，完整证据各4/11；引用16/24、11/20，正确拒答各3/3；完整回答各11/14。[质量评分][E2] | 文档专项数据继续保留；从真实代码任务提取可核对的关键源码/API证据，测错取、漏取及其交付影响。代码导航收益单独验证。 | | 治理与恢复 | 能否拦住越界，同时让合法操作完成；中断后是否重复写入？ | 已知18类/30个组件用例，所选边界错误放行0/14、重复副作用0/5；该历史运行存在全树版本变动，不能签发当前版本统一通过。[治理原件][E3] 另有明确中断点的进程恢复记录，范围见[历次结果](audits/EVALUATION_FIRST_RESULTS_20260926.md#4-治理恢复及受限执行的证据层级)。 | 对当前交付涉及的源码漂移、范围、重复操作和中断点做正反对照；补合法操作误拒绝。模型没修好与平台错误阻断分开归因。 | | 上下文与资源 | 同等交付质量下，调用和等待是否值得？ | 同一配置任务三对均交付；普通/去重复用输入66,655/134,337，平均工具4/7，总Token72,119/140,556；组合策略成本退化后默认关闭。[资源对照][E4] | 每次交付保留原生用量；效率主张再配对比较完成率、每成功任务总成本及逐次耗时。P95按原公式保留，小样本解释为最大值附近的观察。 | | 追踪与定位 | 出错后能否重建事实、找到可操作首因，减少排查返工？ | 指定独立失败样本完整重建2/2。[重建][E5] 本地AI定位对照两臂均0/2正确、有效计时配对0。[定位][E6] | 真实失败保留必要输入/输出和版本；需要定位提速主张时另做固定起点、正确性先行的配对，AI与人工耗时分别记录。 | | 持续迭代 | 改进能否迁移到新任务，既有行为是否退化？ | 原47文件CI选集本地1420通过、2跳过；现选集53文件，后续相关检查分批通过，新版全集及远程CI尚未执行。[CI定义](../.github/workflows/ci.yml)、[检查点](../artifacts/eval_driven_20260928/ci_checkpoint_02/) | 将真实失败转为对应回归；候选整合时跑选定完整范围，新任务冻结后再比较。已有检查范围与实际发布强制范围分别填写。 | | Self-RAG质量反馈 | 质量判断能否减少不可靠输出及无效返工，额外推理是否值得？ | 已有真实标注/筛选/训练/重载（含AI复核样本与合成控制）及14题三臂；固定检索、微调、外部Critic无证据断言分别10/37、57/104、11/38，未取得下降；三臂调用14/28/42。[质量对照][E7] | 保留研究完成事实与负结果。后续针对标签/协议/权重或接受逻辑做小对照；Critic增加“直接重写一次”基线，再用新样本检验质量与总成本。 | RAG的11/14包含合理拒答，引用支持另算；RAG与Self-RAG复用这14题，不是28道独立题。相关语义评分为来源辅助AI审阅，后续正式使用按重要性补领域核对或评分校准。为什么要有它：覆盖证据、引用正确、回答完整和训练效果各有分母，不能互相替代。 跨段用量、人工澄清/救援/批准/环境恢复、人工工时和金额成本，按选定任务的原件或事件补齐；现有工具没有证明自动采集的字段继续留未知。为什么要有它：保留待填的真实需求，同时不把缺少的值补成零。 ## 成功数据怎样读 [EDD成功条件](EVALUATION_DRIVEN_DEVELOPMENT.md#21-单个任务的成功条件)分别定义补丁可用、任务已交付和自主程度。一次完整trial可包含预算内的多次提交和自动修订；首次trial成功不等于首次补丁就正确。下面仅重述[原冻结候选的两题三轮][E1]，不改变原评分： | 问题 | 原样本给出的数据 | 可支持的判断 | | --- | --- | --- | | 首轮完整运行交付多少题？ | 1/2 | 一道题首轮交付，不能推出首个补丁通过率 | | 哪些题曾经成功？ | 至少成功一次1/2；Catalog为1/3次，Transfer为0/3次 | 当前两个题中只有一个曾成功 | | 哪些题每次都成功？ | 三次均成功0/2 | 没有任务达到这组三次重复的全成功条件 | | 所有重复运行合起来怎样？ | 1/6次交付 | 运行级结果，不能写成6道独立题 | | 首次行为失败后修好了多少？ | 三轮汇总：冻结候选0/1（cc3）；冻结基线0/2（cb2、cb3），见[逐运行行为记录][E1] | 条件分母分别为实际进入行为失败的1、2次运行，既非全部6次，也非首轮；机制比较需固定相同失败候选 | 公开开发探针3/4属于部分进展，尚未达到补丁可用；配置任务完成5项检查及Apply/Build支持其既定交付范围。原始记录关于模型来源和介入的说明保留，自主性不能仅由batch的success字段推断。为什么要有它：同一组事实回答不同问题，阶段通过、任务交付、稳定性和人工依赖应分别展示。 ## 最近一次决定：Transfer诊断不默认化 td6普通修订与td7诊断修订均已结束且未交付；各自在三次行为检查中重复相同代码，终止为`PATCH_BEHAVIOR_NO_PROGRESS`。模型调用7/9，输入＋输出Token为31,298/48,345，执行265.220/293.466秒；这是同一已暴露开发题的单轮结果。[双臂原件][E8] 当前保留诊断实验开关且默认关闭。阶段探针曾达到公开3/4，但这一进展未在本次正常入口转化为交付；新实验需要区分具体输入/流程差异，不重复同配置或要求此题先成功才开展其他任务。为什么要有它：把真实结果落实到投入和采用，避免局部成功掩盖端到端失败。 ## 简历叙事的组织方式 当前公开名称：**RepoForge**。 项目概述候选：围绕需求修改与缺陷修复，设计并结合AI编码工具实现源码调查、补丁生成、真实验收和授权交付流程；利用任务运行记录比较完成情况、失败修订、成本及修改边界，推动平台迭代。 主叙事围绕“任务交付、受控执行、数据驱动改进”组织，技术只在解释机制和选型时出现；RAG/Self-RAG放在其已验证用途下。七项详细数据保留在此清单及原件中，简历可按岗位取其中最有支撑的3—5条。为什么要有它：减少技术名词堆叠不等于删掉测量责任，读者应先理解解决什么问题与产生什么结果。 阶段复盘和项目介绍讲清场景、约束、关键难点、技术取舍、失败案例、指标与演进路线。框架或组件要对应它解决的核心问题，并说明未选替代方案的依据；工程判断与实际对照结论分别标注。为什么要有它：技术名称不能单独说明工程价值，也不能把未做过的方案比较补写成选型成绩。 成功率、延迟、成本和数据量均能追到数据集来源与规模、独立任务数、运行次数、统计口径、版本/预算及失败样本；优先引用已有原件和定义。为什么要有它：无法复现或解释分母的数字会降低可信度，已有记录无需在每次开发中重复抄写。 这些维度在阶段总结或对外表述时检查，日常开发只更新变化的事实与决定。为什么要有它：项目叙事需要随真实成果沉淀，不能变成每个修复开始前都要填满的材料清单。 “完成率提升”“成本降低”“定位缩短”“断言率下降”均由同口径对照决定方向；当前负结果可以表述为发现退化并回退，不能填进预设的正向句式。企业节省工时、收入或生产稳定性待有实际使用数据后再写。为什么要有它：成果要经得起追问，不能由技术实现或演示推算业务回报。 ## “合格”的验证对象 下一阶段按选定应用范围检查：能从需求交付完整可验收修改；出现真实失败后能产生有效修订并通过原验收；不同工程/任务类型有可复查结果与重复波动；合法操作与应拒绝操作均经过验证；成本、人工介入和失败过程能追溯。每项的任务清单、适用验收和可接受预算在对应验证前确定。为什么要有它：项目质量由可用性、可靠性、成本和边界共同支撑，测试数量或某个自选百分比不能单独证明成熟。 下一交付周期先取得新增非配置任务的完整交付和真实失败后的有效修订证据，并检查受影响的已成功行为。不同工程的新任务、重复可靠性和七项专项数据继续按其范围验证；外部榜单分数不直接充当本项目合格线。为什么要有它：给开发一个能检验产品变化的近期终点，同时保留完整项目目标。 项目至少说明质量评估、成本/延迟、安全、故障处理、可观测性与生产化边界六个方面的证据及缺口。生产化边界具体到已验证环境、部署/运行范围、依赖和维护条件，未验证部分按实际前提推进。为什么要有它：这些条件决定系统能否在目标场景中交付和维护，演示成功本身不能证明完整生产可用性。 [E1]: documents.title: Qualified local Patch model selection
documents.text: # Qualified local Patch model selection `continue-fresh-patch --qualified-model-routing <routing.json>` is an optional role selector. It consumes existing Patch/Repair execution and verification facts before constructing the worker. It does not run qualification models, change permissions, switch providers after failure, or provide an external-model route. The existing explicit `--ollama-*` path remains available without a qualification gate. New explicit trials also record the worker identity needed for later qualification; an unqualified model can therefore still be tested explicitly. The role is derived by the product entry: an explicit Repair input/verification selection uses `repair`; other Patch continuations use `initial_patch`. Users do not supply a role override. Qualified selection can supply the model, context, output and timeout settings. If an `--ollama-*` value is also supplied, it must match the selected profile exactly; conflicts are rejected without model sends. ## Configuration and existing owners The local routing JSON has exactly `schema_version` (value `qualified_patch_model_routing_v1`) and `routes`. Each supported role maps to one `qualification_ref`, an existing absolute file path plus its exact SHA-256. There is no fallback list or persistent profile database. The qualification document has these fields: | Field | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `schema_version` | `patch_model_qualification_v1` | | `role` | `initial_patch` or `repair` | | `scope` | Exact `target_mod` from the selected FeatureSpec | | `profile` | Exact existing `LocalOllamaInitialPatchProfileV1.to_dict()` | | `model_digest` | Exact Ollama model digest observed during the trials | | `implementation_sha256` | Producer-recorded worker implementation fingerprint | | `worker_policy_sha256` | Hash of the existing worker policy | | `task_suite_ref` | Exact frozen task-definition file reference | | `attempts` | One `case_id` and exact `attempt_ref` per fixed task | | `quality_policy` | Existing `QualityGatePolicy`, for `task_success_rate` only | The task suite has `schema_version=patch_qualification_tasks_v1`, the same `scope`, and `cases`. Each case has `case_id`, explicit `artifact_store_root` and `workspace_root`, an exact `feature_spec_ref`, `expected_check_ids`, and `verification_identity` (`validator_sha256`, `inputs_sha256`, `environment_sha256`, and the recorded `deterministic_reuse_allowed` value). At least three distinct Feature IDs and FeatureSpec hashes are required. Repeated attempts do not add tasks. These are versioned input documents, not proof from a `qualified: true` flag. The resolver validates their file hashes and recomputes each task result from the exact attempt, its final behavior report, its complete matrix, and its Proposal/Review/Dry-run artifacts. The matrix check identities must equal the fixed task definition, not merely agree with their own shortened summary. The last retained provider response must match the stored Patch bytes. The existing native generator and exact-text materializer reconstruct the result from its fixed baseline; its identity must match both the behavior report and the matrix. Missing retained baseline or matrix code identity remains pending. Every required task must pass; a valid schema or deterministic Review cannot hide a final behavior failure. Retrieval metrics are not reused as Patch scores. `model_admission` still owns live model-name/digest validation and the local-only boundary. `QualityGatePolicy` still owns numeric threshold validation. `ArtifactStore.read` validates artifacts; the original continuation canonical hash validates terminal receipts. The role selector does not replace these owners. ## Evidence limits and revalidation New Patch receipts carry `qualification_execution_identity`. Its fingerprint lists the exact worker, continuation, generator, materializer and Graph source files; it does not use Git HEAD or documentation hashes. It does not claim to fingerprint every dependency or the full operating system. Verifier and input versions belong to the explicit per-task verification identity. Missing execution records, legacy receipts without worker fingerprints, incomplete matrices, replayed trials, or version mismatches remain pending. Final behavior failures are not qualified. Missing qualifications never select another model. References are checked again before a qualified model generates. The routing reference participates in the existing attempt identity, preventing an old explicit run from silently becoming a qualified invocation. Cached calls still pass current qualification selection before returning their old result, including callers of the shared continuation API rather than only the CLI. The selection receipt records the role, scoped task outcomes, denominator, profile/digest and evidence references. It explicitly grants neither disclosure nor Apply authority. Existing live-source, exact-diff approval, Build and Runtime rules remain separate. The included tests use synthetic production-path receipts and an HTTP transport stub. They demonstrate the Repair role selector and rejection paths; they do not qualify any installed real model or establish cross-task model performance. No production model qualification configuration is shipped by this change. ## Fixed real-source task preparation and selection `python -m scripts.prepare_patch_eval_suite` prepares and selects task inputs for the existing `continue-fresh-patch` CLI. It does not introduce a service, another queue, or an execution database. `--suite PATH` performs input preflight only; `--select CASE_ID --attempt-id ID` prints the exact existing CLI arguments. Only an explicit additional `--execute` calls that CLI and its real model path. The returned run and attempt receipt references remain the existing result/query interface. This document does not authorize an execution. Preparation takes one explicit `--prepare-seed PATH`. The seed binds an output root, existing P0 CLI arguments, the unchanged original P0 matrix, and the files that identify its validator, source input and execution environment. Existing output directories are not overwritten. The result uses the already-supported `patch_qualification_tasks_v1` schema and can be consumed as `task_suite_ref` by the qualification resolver after independent real trials exist. The first dataset defines three distinct AccurateCrosshair Feature tasks: | Task | Scope and independent oracle | | --- | --- | | `accurate-crosshair-recoil-default-off` | A newly defined Eval request, not a change to the user's production request. Fresh Follow Recoil defaults false; explicit true/false, five other defaults and configuration keys are preserved. Five checks across three C# processes. | | `accurate-crosshair-spread-api-input-validation` | A newly defined public Mod API request. Negative/non-finite modifiers throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` without changing state or callback count; finite non-negative input, replacement, removal and notification semantics remain. Seventeen checks across five C# processes. | | `accurate-crosshair-spread-toggle` | The existing P0 Feature and Plan, counted once. Reuses its original 36-check matrix; prospective verification identity is added to new report copies without rewriting historical reports or changing expected results. | The two new input Plans and source-support judgments are explicitly operator authored. Their requests and checks are fixed before any product model attempt. They qualify only the Patch role being measured, not autonomous Evidence or Planning. Repeating P0 in Repair mode does not create another Feature task or increase the denominator. All new task trials start as `not_run`; baseline oracle runs and successful input preflight do not count as model successes. Evidence levels remain separate: 1. Synthetic contract tests validate selection, rejection and record binding. 2. Real original C# source with explicit dependency/engine doubles validates the selected local behavior. Compiler, references and runtime are fixed; this is not a complete host/OS reproducibility claim. 3. Real-model task trials must retain original responses, behavior matrices and the Proposal/Review/Dry-run chain before A7 can qualify a profile. 4. DSH/service operation and GTFO Runtime remain separate, unexecuted acceptance layers. Neither is implied by this task dataset.

documents.title: WallCrawler leakage audit
documents.text: authority: non_authoritative_derived_presentation # WallCrawler leakage audit - The request contains no complete Hook identity or expected product blocker. - The actual retrieval scope is an allowlist of `Assets/Scripts/Modules-ASM` and `Datablocks` under the supplied R8 root. - Natural API identifiers inside those roots are legitimate source facts. - Historical implementation, technical annotation, evidence projection, project/queue documents, fixed-answer tests, prior Agent/RAG output, and product diagnostic outputs are explicitly excluded from actual retrieval. - Exact IL coverage is an evidence input; it does not label any method acceptable. - `GTFOR8EvidenceProvider` readiness, `can_generate_patch`, blocker codes, and other product diagnostics are outside the actual and expected owners. - The validator checks the request for the fixture's fixed complete-answer literals and verifies the manifest allowlist and excluded source classes. This is a fixture-bound leakage check, not an expected judgment, held-out, promotion, RAG-quality, or Data Readiness claim.

documents.title: Non-authoritative Projection Interface Checkpoint
documents.text: # Non-authoritative Projection Interface Checkpoint Status: accepted corrective code/test checkpoint integrated on `codex/rag-capability-mainline` Accepted source lineage: `4469279de886f5eba22d451dd215837c3e8fc389 -> 889ecd54e51db4d0882df0c4cc2b0d66850fb167 -> be8a91077e0ec28fdbf72ee5d5fa063f700ed41a` Integrated mainline lineage: `c2c8e31abaed1b795d61c5b62e5d39defcb984da -> 7576d86853f77acba6b73f5ace07e4ccb3755297 -> 36d51d897ab6d329c5efac7d6012d8837d9cd772` Responsibility authority: `docs/audits/NON_AUTHORITATIVE_PROJECTION_RESPONSIBILITY_BOUNDARY_20260830.md` This checkpoint freezes one read-only, rebuildable interface for Thin Lineage, owner-test migration, a future Langfuse exporter, and ProjectionRebuild. It does not merge either rejected whole-commit design and does not create an Artifact, Graph branch, Approval, Gateway, queue, fact owner, production consumer, or execution decision. ## 1. Exact public surface and owner-fact admission The independent package is `src.non_authoritative_projection`. It uses only the Python standard library and its own modules. Its public surface is: - `FactRefV1` - `OwnerFactV1` - `EdgeReporterV1` - `ExplicitEdgeV1` - `ProjectionDiagnosticV1` - `ProjectionViewV1` - `ProjectionContractError` - the frozen admission, relation, direction, diagnostic-code, and schema-version constants `OwnerFactV1` has exactly these fields, in this serialized order: 1. `schema_version` 2. `owner` 3. `fact_type` 4. `fact_ref` 5. `payload_sha256` 6. `payload_schema_version` 7. `owner_sequence` It contains no owner payload and no extensible metadata map. Admission is the closed, versioned `owner_fact_admission_v1` table: | `owner` | `fact_type` | payload schema | sequence mode | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `artifact_store` | `artifact_revision_v1` | exact `1.0` | `unavailable`; serialized only as `null`; cannot report an edge | | `product_execution` | `product_execution_output_v1` | exact `1.0` | `required`; exact integer `>= 0` | Callers cannot register a pair. `OwnerFactV1` validates the table in its constructor and `from_dict`; `FactRefV1` rejects owners outside the table. Unknown owners, responsibility owners not admitted by this checkpoint, cross-paired fact types, status/claim-like fact types, wrong payload schema, and invented/missing sequence values fail before a View can accept them. ### 1.1 Exact current owner field sources `product_execution/product_execution_output_v1` is admitted only for one Artifact output contained in a completely returned and strictly replayable `ProductExecutionResultV1`: | projection field | current owner source | | --- | --- | | `fact_ref` | `ProductExecutionOutputV1.artifact_ref.path` | | `payload_sha256` | `ProductExecutionOutputV1.artifact_ref.artifact_hash` | | `payload_schema_version` | the matching validated output-readback envelope's `schema_version` | | `owner_sequence` | `ProductExecutionOutputV1.sequence` | The current ProductExecution strict replay already binds the output ref/hash to the matching output-readback envelope. The projection test copies these fields only after `execute_product_execution` returns. `artifact_store/artifact_revision_v1` is admitted from one immutable revision: | projection field | current owner source | | --- | --- | | `fact_ref` | `ArtifactRef.path` | | `payload_sha256` | `ArtifactRef.artifact_hash`, equal to `ArtifactEnvelope.artifact_hash` | | `payload_schema_version` | `ArtifactEnvelope.schema_version` | | `owner_sequence` | `null`; ArtifactStore exposes no revision-local integer sequence | The missing ArtifactStore sequence is represented, not fabricated. The admission table makes this pair endpoint-only, so a caller cannot put `0` in the field and use it as an edge reporter. ## 2. Explicit exclusions The table is deliberately smaller than the responsibility-owner list: | excluded owner/fact | exact missing representation | | --- | --- | | `EntryAdmissionResultV1` / `EntryAdmissionRunV1` | no exact owner-local integer sequence tied to the receipt ref/hash/schema | | `ActualRunResultV1` | journal ref/hash exist, but the result has no contract/schema version and no exact owner-local integer sequence; `actual_attempt_id` is not parsed into one | | top-level `ProductExecutionResultV1` | no exact fact ref, payload hash, or owner-local sequence | | LangGraph `TraceEvent` / `ModAgentState` | no single owner-issued schema, payload hash, and owner-local sequence tuple | | `BuildResult` | no owner-issued fact ref, payload hash, schema version, or owner-local sequence | | Runtime evidence payload builders | no frozen Runtime owner-result contract carrying the complete tuple | | human exact-diff and authority decisions | no current owner record carrying the complete ref/hash/schema/owner-local sequence tuple | No fixture value, concatenated identity, parsed numeric suffix, status, claim, or default `0` substitutes for these missing owner fields. ## 3. Explicit edge semantics Each endpoint is an exact `FactRefV1` containing `owner` and `fact_ref`. `EdgeReporterV1` binds the source fact's full `FactRefV1`, exact `payload_sha256`, and exact `owner_sequence`. The interface mechanically enforces `reporter.fact == source`. There is no third-party reporter form. Source is therefore both the directional source endpoint and the fact that explicitly signs the relation; target is only the directional target endpoint. Rebuild checks that source/reporter and target facts exist and that reporter hash and sequence equal the admitted source fact. The finite relations and exact directions are: | `relation` | direction | | --- | --- | | `references` | source is the reporter fact explicitly signing source -> target as a reference | | `derived_from` | source is the reporter fact explicitly signing source as derived from target | | `caused_by` | source is the reporter fact explicitly signing source as caused by target | | `conflicts_with` | source is the reporter fact explicitly signing a conflict with target; direction conveys no priority | No relation is inferred from a timestamp, input order, write order, path, filename, similar identifier, owner sequence, or payload hash. ## 4. Rebuild, serialization, and diagnostics `ProjectionViewV1.rebuild(facts, edges)` treats collection order as non-semantic, rejects duplicate fact refs and duplicate edges, sorts only for serialization, and derives every diagnostic from the complete supplied facts and edges. Facts sort by `(owner, fact_ref)`. Edges sort by their exact endpoint, relation, and source-reporter binding fields. Diagnostics sort by canonical bytes. These sort orders are not an event order, cross-owner order, causal order, failure order, or priority order. `owner_sequence` is never compared between different owners. Canonical bytes are compact UTF-8 JSON with exact contract field order, `ensure_ascii=False`, `allow_nan=False`, and separators `(',', ':')`. `canonical_sha256()` hashes those bytes as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. `from_dict` accepts only canonical field and collection order. Unknown fields, reordered fields or collections, duplicate refs, duplicate edges, duplicate diagnostics, malformed hashes, unsupported versions, unadmitted owner/fact pairs, unsupported relations, and diagnostics not exactly regenerated from the inputs all fail explicitly. The diagnostic codes remain item-level only: - `missing_source_fact` - `missing_target_fact` - `missing_reporter_fact` - `reporter_payload_sha256_mismatch` - `reporter_owner_sequence_mismatch` - `explicit_conflict` A valid cross-owner `conflicts_with` edge retains both facts and produces one `explicit_conflict` diagnostic. It does not select a winner. There is no aggregate projection-integrity result, product status, route result, retry decision, failure chain, first-failure result, claim-impact result, or authorization field. ## 5. No observer and no production consumer The synchronous ProductExecutor callback added by the original checkpoint is removed. `execute_product_execution` has no projection/callback parameter and `src.mod_agent.product_executor` does not import this package. An arbitrary callable could capture Store, Graph, files, network clients, or process-control capabilities through a closure; copying only the result object cannot prove capability or Store isolation. The invariance test instead performs this sequence: ```text execute_product_execution returns completely -> copy exact fields from current owner contracts into admitted facts -> snapshot the complete ProductExecutionResult and Store revisions -> call pure ProjectionViewV1.rebuild for normal input -> call pure ProjectionViewV1.rebuild for missing input -> call pure ProjectionViewV1.rebuild for cross-owner conflict input -> compare the unchanged owner result, Graph count, Store counters, refs, paths, and bytes ``` There is no production consumer, callback, file writer, network exporter, or runtime integration in this checkpoint. ## 6. Dependency and capability isolation The dependency direction is: ```text owner contracts / immutable owner results | external owner-specific adapter v src.non_authoritative_projection | read-only future consumers ``` `src.mod_agent` remains on the forbidden side of the reverse dependency guard. The guard resolves absolute and relative imports across every current and future Python module under `src/mod_agent`; it does not reject the separate existing `src.observability` package. The projection package's dependency allowlist contains only `__future__`, `collections`, `dataclasses`, `hashlib`, `json`, `typing`, and its own package. It cannot import Graph, Actual execution, ArtifactStore, ProductExecution, Repair, Apply, UI, Langfuse, tests, or another product module. ## 7. Verification evidence All commands use repository test doubles. No real model, network, product preflight, packet, Actual, Build, Apply, Repair, or Runtime operation is started. | command | result | | --- | --- | | `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_non_authoritative_projection.py tests/unit/test_non_authoritative_projection_boundary.py tests/unit/test_product_execution.py -k "non_authoritative or external_post_return or no_projection_callback" -q` | `42 passed, 105 deselected` | | `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_product_execution.py -q` | `107 passed` | | `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_workflow_graph.py -q` | `135 passed` | The post-return test snapshots complete ProductExecutionResult canonical bytes, terminal, blockers, Store-attempt sequence, effect-event sequence, every output Artifact ref/hash, Graph invocation count, Store read/write counters, and each immutable revision's exact path and complete bytes.
